C.Drive by Chaos Custom Shop | RockBoard | PedalPedia Skip to main content LOG IN EXPLORE Chaos Custom Shop C.Drive LOG IN TO SUGGEST IMPROVEMENTS OVERDRIVE Description Designed as a refined twist on the legendary Klon Centaur, the Chaos Custom Shop C.Drive offers a thick, smooth overdrive that remains balanced and musical. It blends clean and driven signals seamlessly, allowing for subtle coloration at low gain settings up to rich overdrive. The pedal features three mini‑toggle switches allowing control over EQ range, clipping style (symmetry), and added low‑end fatness to compensate for the traditional Klon’s bass limitations. Housed in a robust metal enclosure and built with true‑bypass switching and high‑quality branded components, it is handcrafted in Poland. Power draw is minimal and the response is dynamic and touch‑sensitive. What's missing here? We know that this pedal exists, but not much more. You can change that by submitting improvements to this pedal! Don't worry, it's quick and easy with our Pedal Creator. - **Archive parent:** C.Drive
- **Builder:** Chaos Custom Shop / Chaos FX
- **Catalog type:** Overdrive
- **Identity:** Klon Centaur-inspired analog overdrive with three independent voicing switches for EQ range, clipping symmetry and low-end fatness. [1][2]

- **GAIN**
- **TONE**
- **LEVEL**
- **EQ:** Three-position frequency-range selector.
- **SYM:** Three-position clipping-symmetry selector.
- **FAT:** Adds low-end content. [1][2]

- **Primary reference:** Klon Centaur.
- The design is a Klon-style interpretation with additional selectable clipping/EQ behavior, not a claim of identical historical components. [1]

- Exact production transistor/device part number is not publicly documented.

- **SYM** provides selectable symmetrical/asymmetrical clipping behavior.
- Exact diode part numbers are not documented. [1][2]

- Exact model-specific voltage/current figures are not securely preserved in the reviewed sources.

- Analog signal path.
- Handcrafted in Poland. [1]

- **C.Drive** is the archive identity.
- Contemporary listings also use **C.Drive+**, but the evidence does not establish a complete revision history, so the names are not silently merged.

The pedal is intended to retain the balanced boost/overdrive response associated with the Klon family while allowing substantial changes to clipping symmetry and low-end content. EQ and Fat broaden the range beyond the traditional three-knob Klon interface. [1][2]

- **Identity:** High
- **Klon lineage:** High
- **Three voicing switches:** High
- **Symmetrical/asymmetrical clipping:** High
- **Polish handcrafted construction:** High
- **Exact components:** Unknown

RockBoard PedalPedia and an exact C.Drive+ Reverb record were cross-checked. The sources agree on the C.Drive identity, Klon lineage, selectable clipping/EQ/fatness functions and Polish construction. [1][2]

boost/overdrive/fuzz), Hexe Guitar Electronics (Piotr Zapart — BitCrusher III, reVOLVER), LongAmp (Roxanne Electric Mistress clone), Occvlt (Amethyst Dope Fuzz), Sitek (Pandora Fuzz), Exar Electronix (defunked; Series 1–5 lineage, SF‑04 Super Fuzz), Taurus Amplification (Stomp‑Head 1.VT 40W Vintage floor tube amp) and Yankee Power (HS‑M5 compact; HS‑M24 flagship adjustable power supply). Many brands sell via Reverb.com; some ranges (Pue, Visar) are defunked. Coverage spans amps, fuzz, overdrive, delay, reverb, modulation and power supplies. Hunt Exar rarities on Reverb; for electrical or modification issues consult a qualified tech. Poland was both trickier and yet eventually easier to rationalise than originally perceived. I have scanned through many a country now, and Poland seems to be the last of those with sufficient numbers of high calibre pedal builders to warrant a dedicated feature*. As noted before - these sorts of article take quite a lot of work to complete - and so this is the last of these I will be doing for a while. * Note that USA and Japan are the leading pedal builders of the world still and too large for these individual country-focus features - most of the pedals in my collection are American or Japanese - as are most of those featured on this site - so this is more about giving exposure to some of the lesser-known brands! It completes the cycle started with Best of British , then Canadian , French , German , Italian , Greek , Spanish , Danish , Swedish/Finnish/Norwegian - and now finally Polish - a nicely rounded 10 all told and sort of coincidentally European. When I touch on this sort of thing again I will likely do a continental or more global overview - listing less well known but still leading/interesting pedal innovators from further afield around the world.
